title: L1 Mid-Review: Build-A-Bot
story: You're building an AI assistant — a friendly bot that greets users, asks them questions, analyzes their answers, gives personalized advice, and says goodbye. It's not magic; it's just functions working together. Here's what you can make with everything you've learned.
why: This capstone lesson combines 6+ functions into a cohesive program, demonstrating that real applications are built by composing many small, focused functions.
analogy: Build-A-Bot is like assembling a robot from modules. The greeting module says hello, the mood module reads emotions, the advice module dispenses wisdom, and the farewell module says goodbye. Each module (function) plugs into the main control board (main function). Add a new module and your robot gains a new skill.
try_it: Add two new capabilities to Bot-Kilo: a `tell_joke() -> Str` function that picks a random joke from a list, and a `rate_day(rating: Int) -> Str` function that comments on a day rating from 1 to 10.
tips: Each function handles ONE bot capability — don't mix greeting with advice
main() is the conductor: it calls functions in order and passes data between them
Start by writing and testing each function independently before wiring them together
Use the patterns from earlier lessons: if/elif for analysis, random_range for variety, str_len for inspection
common_mistakes: Writing everything in main() instead of delegating to functions
Creating functions but never calling them from main()
Making functions too big — if a function does two different things, split it
Forgetting return types on functions that produce values
